_doc: Term 1-4 Level 1 (term/l1) tool of the day, one row per lesson 1-40. Wording of tool names and definitions comes ONLY from levels/spine.json (band A, ages 6-8); this file holds the choice, the role (I introduce, P practise, A apply, C choose), a one-line reason (tutor guide only, never printed for children) and, for choose lessons, 'lean_now': what the current content leans on (tutor guide note only). Design: term/l1/SPINE_TERM_DESIGN.md. Applied to lesson files by term/l1/tools/apply_spine_term.py.
choose_note: Lessons 10, 20, 30 and 40 are choose-the-tool lessons (owner decision 2, consolidation). Lesson 39 (The Problem-Solving Toolbox) is also marked choose because its whole job is picking the tool; the owner may set it to a single tool instead. Until the consolidation plan moves the new ideas out of 10, 20 and 30, those lessons still teach Story Steps, Find One First and Calendar Detective; the tool chip says 'Choose one' and lean_now tells the tutor which tools the content leans on.

look_back.say: Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one word, or pass. Still stuck? Tick the box and ask your grown-up to photograph this page.
look_back.do: Children fill in the look-back box on page 5. Nobody reads theirs out. Praise a check you saw, not speed.

script.opening_do: Point at the tool on page 1 of the workbook.
script.choose_do: Point at the row of eight tools on page 1 of the workbook.
script.choose_note: Optional, no time modelled: ask which tool the group chose and why. Volunteers first; listen for a tool being named and a reason.
script.talk_note: Listen for the tool being named, not the answer. Volunteers first, a pass is always fine.
script.kit_note: Eight tools: see your Toolbox card. Point at it when you point at the tool on page 1. If the card is not printed, send the PDF with the welcome message.

1.title: Bundles and Singles
1.reason: Children bundle real sticks first; Start here then asks them to draw bundles and singles.

2.title: Number Words and the Number Line
2.reason: Every Start here item sits on a number line, and the frog hops are acted out before they are drawn.

3.title: Digit Cards
3.reason: Children make every number from two cards in order, then from three cards, then from four.

4.title: The 100 Square Explorer
4.reason: Colouring 10s, 5s and 2s and moving a counter down the square shows what repeats and what grows.

5.title: Make-a-Ten Adding
5.reason: Counters move on ten-frames to fill a ten; 8 + 6 comes before 28 + 6.

6.title: Tens Jump, Ones Hop
6.reason: Every sum is drawn as jumps and hops on a number line; Think harder asks where Ali started.

7.title: Take Away, Count Up
7.reason: Counting up and adding back undo a take-away, and this is where children first check an answer another way.

8.title: Balance and Swap
8.reason: Children move real small things between two plates and see what stays equal.

9.title: Draw and Measure
9.reason: Every task is drawn to size (a 7 cm line, a bent path); children measure real things first.

10.title: Story Steps: Read It Twice
10.reason: Choose-the-tool lesson. For now the content leans on counters (Act it out) and drawing each step.

11.title: Who Is Where?
11.reason: Children stand toys in a line and touch each place; Think harder and Go further are drawn.

12.title: Bar Strips: More and Fewer
12.reason: The strip is the picture of the story; sum-and-difference items are solved by undoing the gap.

13.title: Doubles and Near Doubles
13.reason: Each near double is one more or one less than a double; counters show the extra one.

14.title: Odd + Odd: Always, Sometimes, Never
14.reason: Counters in pairs show why odd and even behave as they do; then children test many sums.

15.title: Equal Groups
15.reason: Groups, number in each group and total go in a table; plates are drawn and ways to group 12 are listed.

16.title: Skip-Count Tables
16.reason: Last digits of the 2s, 5s and 10s repeat; a counter hops along the line as the frog.

17.title: Sharing and Grouping
17.reason: Children deal counters onto plates; Go further lists every number of friends that share 12.

18.title: Times Stories
18.reason: Equal strips show 'twice as many'; the hidden-unit items are solved by undoing the total.

19.title: Picture Equations
19.reason: Try a number for each shape, then check it in every line; the Investigation lists the pairs that fit.

20.title: Find One First
20.reason: Choose-the-tool lesson. For now the content leans on a strip (Draw it) and a table of prices.

21.title: What Time Is It?
21.reason: The long hand counts in 5s round the face; the kit clock is set and moved by hand.

22.title: Five Minutes at a Time
22.reason: Hands and 5-minute steps are drawn on a clock and a time line; counting in 5s is the helper.

23.title: Time Passes
23.reason: From the end time, count back to find the start; a time line shows the jumps.

24.title: Dollars and Change
24.reason: Children list the ways to make an amount, try sets for the fewest coins, and find a price from change.

25.title: Price Tags: Compare and Choose
25.reason: Try two tags, check the total or the gap, then try again; strips show how much more.

26.title: The School Shop
26.reason: Every way to spend exactly $20 is listed in order, with a row for each number of books.

27.title: Fill the Grid
27.reason: Place a tile, check its row and column, and change it if it breaks a rule.

28.title: Make a Table
28.reason: A table of sticks per picture finds the 10th picture; Go further works back from a total.

29.title: Spot the Mistake
29.reason: Add back, or take away, to check a sum; a rough sum with friendly numbers shows if the answer is about right.

30.title: Calendar Detective
30.reason: Choose-the-tool lesson. For now the content leans on the cycle of 7 (Spot the pattern) and counting on.

31.title: Half and Quarter
31.reason: Children cut and colour shapes in equal parts; from one quarter they work back to the whole.

32.title: Build the Figure
32.reason: Shapes in a figure are counted by kind into a table; a ruler splits a figure into its shapes.

33.title: Copy on the Grid
33.reason: Routes are listed in order so none is missed; the 3 by 1 and 2 by 2 grids come before bigger ones.

34.title: Cubes and Views
34.reason: Children build the stack and fold and punch real paper; top views are drawn.

35.title: Spot It
35.reason: Tiles repeat and a missing piece follows the pattern; cards are turned and compared by hand.

36.title: Count Everything
36.reason: Handshakes among 2, 3, then 4 children, and squares in 1 by 1 then 2 by 2 grids, show how the count grows.

37.title: Make Your Own Graph
37.reason: Tally marks go into a table before the graph; a missing bar comes from the total.

38.title: Graph Detectives
38.reason: A missing bar is the total take away the bars you know; graphs are drawn from clues.

39.title: The Problem-Solving Toolbox
39.reason: Choose-the-tool lesson. Its tool cards still use the lesson's own seven names; see the design note.

40.title: Inquirers' Showcase
40.reason: Choose-the-tool lesson. Children teach their favourite idea and pick the tool that fits.
